Calculation and input workshop

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the design chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Legacy console practice. These slides are not the current Pygame Task 1. Use the aligned game chapter and workbook. Replacement project slides are pending (A06).

1. Calculation and input workshop

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Connect validated input to a tested cost calculation. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

Zero is valid and costs zero cents. Conversion and range checks belong at the input boundary. A calculation function receives a validated quantity. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

3. The order contract

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Use the project requirements. Keep prices in integer cents. No need to add accounts or a new interface. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

4. Predicted costs

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

Expected costs are 0, 300 and 1200 cents. Ask learners to predict before running. The calculation assumes successful validation. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

5. Retry trace

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Conversion fails for three. Negative one converts but fails the range rule. Zero is accepted and costs zero. Use driver/navigator roles, then swap. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Use a separate project copy. Accept equivalent function names. Check the retry loop actually continues and the calculation returns a value. Support with the chapter example, then ask for an independent changed input. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

B. Printing displays text. A normally completed call without an explicit returned value gives None. Ask what cost = order_cost(4) would store. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

Look for successful conversion, accepted range, returned zero cost and actual retest evidence. Keep storage integration for the next workshop. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
